generation.forced_text:
The Jet stream

Hey guys! So let’s imagine there’s some super cool air flowing from really high in altitude. We could picture something a whole mile in thickness, like that giant blue ribbon stretching over North and North America! And, guesswhat! The wind in that cool ribbon blows super speedy! We refer the cool, breezesy ribbon up above us like this—The **" Jet-stream. ” 

So now you see this ribbon-like jetstream, how do it move the temperature from cold place up in North Canada towards warm places, such the Southern Uplines.  When that cool ribbon dips or curves down south it’s like that air is moving south and bringing colder temperature with, and similarly if this ribbon rises, or it curves north that is warm temperature from further to south up.  And it doesn’t always move smoothly
